mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.0 Z-score) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.5 Z-score) in at least 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below the previous 12-month average indicates a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with disinflation, which historically precedes equity market corrections and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while CPIAUCSL < 12-month moving average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.7 Z-score) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (>0.5 Z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) month-over-month indicates a paradoxical labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, foreshadowing earnings downgrades and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises while PAYEMS also rises month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.6 Z-score) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (implied by rising RSAFS and stable CPIAUCSL) above 0.4% for six consecutive months signals improving household purchasing power, which drives higher consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises >0.4% monthly while CPIAUCSL change is within ±0.2% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (>0.7 Z-score) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
